The NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 is out now. Priced at $1000 it includes all the new GeForce RTX 50 features and offers good gaming performance. On the other hand, the gen-over-gen performance increase is smaller than expected, but NVIDIA didn't raise their pricing either.
The 980 was $549 in 2014, which seems to be about $730 today. That means the 5080 at $999 is 1.3x the price of the 980. Yet the geometric mean score is 8.5x.

It's neat to see the 4080 Super doing well compared to the 5080 and 5090. It's clearly behind them in many cases, but seems to have better performance per watt ratio than them while also having some of the lowest temps.
